newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia sees its 1997 tourism income at $120 mln.
newsitem.headline: Serbia sees its 1997 tourism income at $120 mln.

text.p: Serbia plans to triple its tourism earnings in 1997 to $120 million, the Belgrade daily Politika reported on Friday.
Serbia earned around $40 million from tourism in 1996, the paper said.

The planned surge in tourism revenue is based mainly on the country's economic stability and measures taken by the federal and the republican governments, Politika said quoting deputy Minister of Tourism Radisav Stankovic.

"The republican government plans to earmark around two million dinars ($389,924) for tourist propaganda, but the federal government would have to provide a lot more for the same purpose," Stankovic was quoted as saying.
In 1996, the government collected around 440 million dinars from the exit tax, paid by Yugoslavs travelling abroad, but almost none of it went for tourism.

"This year we shall require at least half of the 550 million dinars planned from the exit tax to be invested in promoting tourism," Stankovic said. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
